scope: Engineering diagnosis only; no new production, provider calls, changes to installed package, failed attempt recovery, or release. A separate cloned Workspace was instrumented with an external preload that records and rethrows the original calls.
finding: The controller-added macOS sandbox-exec wrapper prevents /bin/ps from starting. An intermittent post-close process-group EPERM invokes the existing ps fallback, which also receives EPERM under that wrapper. The boolean fallback drops the inspection exception and the CLI reports only the original kill error.
causalChain: Browser render child exits with status 0.
Immediate group SIGKILL and signal 0 both return EPERM.
Fallback execFileSync(/bin/ps) fails immediately with spawnSync /bin/ps EPERM.
Inspection returns false and the original cleanup EPERM fails doctor.
Worker records task failure; fixed continuation cannot deliver.
testIsolationOwner: Acceptance controller, not Hermes or the ordinary npm Workspace
nodeObservation: Hermes terminal login resolves Node v26.4.0; simple non-login shell resolves Node v22.22.3. Host/sandbox Hermes controls both used v26.4.0, so Node version was not changed in the causal comparison.
correction: Repeated worker doctor increases the number of checks but is not the demonstrated root cause; failure also reproduced serially. Native delegate_task compatibility is not disproven by this failure. The existing host cleanup fallback succeeded in all three observed host runs that required ps.
limitations: The original production log did not retain the ps exception. The same error branch was captured in a new reproduction with the same candidate and equivalent sandbox policy.
Eight successful host doctor runs are not a completed Hermes video or a new black-box first-use receipt.
A corrected isolation strategy must preserve first-use context independence without disabling required host capabilities; do not relabel an unrestricted diagnostic as isolated acceptance.
remainingWork: Correct the acceptance isolation design and preflight all required host capabilities, including the cleanup fallback.
Expose sanitized inspection failure reasons in runtime diagnostics.
Clarify Root versus worker readiness responsibilities.
Repeat fresh candidate and post-release npm acceptance before declaring stable release.
